GCS-Compatible Object Store Support

pgBackRest supports repositories in GCS-compatible object stores. Create the bucket first; pgBackRest does not create it. You can use the bucket root (/). Usually, prefer a subpath so object-store logs and other data can share the bucket without conflicts.

pg-primary:/etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf ⇒ Configure GCS

[demo]
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data
[global]
process-max=4
repo1-block=y
repo1-bundle=y
repo1-cipher-pass=zWaf6XtpjIVZC5444yXB+cgFDFl7MxGlgkZSaoPvTGirhPygu4jOKOXf9LO4vjfO
repo1-cipher-type=aes-256-cbc
repo1-path=/var/lib/pgbackrest
repo1-retention-diff=2
repo1-retention-full=2
repo2-azure-account=pgbackrest
repo2-azure-container=demo-container
repo2-azure-key=YXpLZXk=
repo2-path=/demo-repo
repo2-retention-full=4
repo2-type=azure
repo3-path=/demo-repo
repo3-retention-full=4
repo3-s3-bucket=demo-bucket
repo3-s3-endpoint=s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
repo3-s3-key=accessKey1
repo3-s3-key-secret=verySecretKey1
repo3-s3-region=us-east-1
repo3-type=s3
repo4-bundle=y
repo4-path=/demo-repo
repo4-sftp-host=sftp-server
repo4-sftp-host-key-hash-type=sha1
repo4-sftp-host-user=pgbackrest
repo4-sftp-private-key-file=/var/lib/pgsql/.ssh/id_rsa_sftp
repo4-sftp-public-key-file=/var/lib/pgsql/.ssh/id_rsa_sftp.pub
repo4-type=sftp
repo5-gcs-bucket=demo-bucket
repo5-gcs-key=/etc/pgbackrest/gcs-key.json
repo5-path=/demo-repo
repo5-type=gcs
start-fast=y
[global:archive-push]
compress-level=3

On GCE, set repo5-gcs-key-type=auto to authenticate through the instance service account.

Run commands as you would for a repository on a local disk.

GCS file creation is relatively slow. Enable file bundling to improve backup/restore performance.

Target Time for Repository

Set the point in time at which commands read a repository on versioned storage. This lets you recover data deleted or corrupted by user error or malware.

S3, GCS, and Azure support versioned storage, but usually disable it by default. In addition to versioning, consider S3 object locking or GCS and Azure soft delete.

When you specify repo-target-time, you must also specify repo. Some repository types probably will not support versioning. Recovery usually targets one repository.

Storage timestamps must be <= the specified timestamp. pgBackRest truncates milliseconds from the specified timestamp.

Delete the S3 repository demo stanza to demonstrate recovery from versioned storage.

pg-primary ⇒ Delete stanza in S3 repository

sudo systemctl stop postgresql-14.service
sudo -u postgres pgbackrest --stanza=demo stop
sudo -u postgres pgbackrest --stanza=demo --repo=3 stanza-delete

After deletion, info reports a repository error.

pg-primary ⇒ Error on info

sudo -u postgres pgbackrest --stanza=demo --repo=3 info
stanza: demo

    status: error (missing stanza path)

Versioned storage lets you read the repository before deletion. Finding the target time can be difficult. Here, use the deletion time of backup.info to identify when the stanza was deleted.

pg-primary ⇒ List versions of backup.info in the bucket

key=demo-repo/backup/demo/backup.info; \
       aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket demo-bucket \
       --prefix $key --output table \
       --query "sort_by([Versions[?Key=='$key'].{Action:'PUT', \
       Modified:LastModified,Object:Key}, \
       DeleteMarkers[?Key=='$key'].{Action:'DELETE', \
       Modified:LastModified,Object:Key}][],&Modified)"
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
|                                ListObjectVersions                                 |
+--------+------------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
| Action |             Modified               |               Object                |
+--------+------------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
|  PUT   |  2026-09-27T10:11:25.317000+00:00  |  demo-repo/backup/demo/backup.info  |
|  PUT   |  2026-09-27T10:11:38.216000+00:00  |  demo-repo/backup/demo/backup.info  |
|  DELETE|  2026-09-27T10:11:50.305000+00:00  |  demo-repo/backup/demo/backup.info  |
+--------+------------------------------------+-------------------------------------+

Run info with a target time before deletion to view the repository.

pg-primary ⇒ Info with target time

sudo -u postgres pgbackrest --stanza=demo --repo=3 \
       --repo-target-time="2026-09-27 10:11:38+00" info
       [filtered 5 lines of output]
        wal archive min/max (14): 00000005000000000000001C/00000005000000000000001D
        full backup: 20260927-101125F
            timestamp start/stop: 2026-09-27 10:11:25+00 / 2026-09-27 10:11:37+00
            wal start/stop: 00000005000000000000001D / 00000005000000000000001D
            repo3: backup set size: 4.2MB, backup size: 4.2MB

If info shows the required backup, restore it with the same target time.

pg-primary ⇒ Restore with target time

sudo -u postgres pgbackrest --stanza=demo --repo=3 --delta \
       --repo-target-time="2026-09-27 10:11:38+00" --log-level-console=info restore
P00   INFO: restore command begin 2.59.2: --delta --exec-id=5687-73aa017d --log-level-console=info --no-log-timestamp --pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data --process-max=4 --repo=3 --repo2-azure-account=<redacted> --repo2-azure-container=demo-container --repo2-azure-key=<redacted> --repo1-cipher-pass=<redacted> --repo1-cipher-type=aes-256-cbc --repo5-gcs-bucket=demo-bucket --repo5-gcs-key=<redacted> --repo1-path=/var/lib/pgbackrest --repo2-path=/demo-repo --repo3-path=/demo-repo --repo4-path=/demo-repo --repo5-path=/demo-repo --repo3-s3-bucket=demo-bucket --repo3-s3-endpoint=s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com --repo3-s3-key=<redacted> --repo3-s3-key-secret=<redacted> --repo3-s3-region=us-east-1 --repo4-sftp-host=sftp-server --repo4-sftp-host-key-hash-type=sha1 --repo4-sftp-host-user=pgbackrest --repo4-sftp-private-key-file=/var/lib/pgsql/.ssh/id_rsa_sftp --repo4-sftp-public-key-file=/var/lib/pgsql/.ssh/id_rsa_sftp.pub --repo-target-time="2026-09-27 10:11:38+00" --repo2-type=azure --repo3-type=s3 --repo4-type=sftp --repo5-type=gcs --stanza=demo
P00   INFO: repo3: restore backup set 20260927-101125F, recovery will start at 2026-09-27 10:11:25

P00   INFO: remove invalid files/links/paths from '/var/lib/pgsql/14/data'
P00   INFO: write updated /var/lib/pgsql/14/data/postgresql.auto.conf
       [filtered 2 lines of output]
sudo systemctl start postgresql-14.service

Dedicated Repository Host

Quickstart suits simple installations. Enterprise installations commonly use a separate repository host for backups and WAL archives. This reduces the effect of database host failures on backup data. Also consider conventional backup software for the repository host.

On each PostgreSQL host, set pg1-path to the local cluster path and leave pg1-host unset. On the repository host, configure pg-host connections to the primary and any standby hosts. Only the repository host configuration should list multiple PostgreSQL hosts. Either index can identify the primary or standby; for example, pg1-path/pg1-host and pg2-path/pg2-host can appear in either order.

Installation

Create a host named repository to store cluster backups.

NOTE:

The pgBackRest version installed on the repository host must exactly match the version installed on the PostgreSQL host.

Create pgbackrest as the repository owner. Any user can own it, but avoid postgres, if present, to prevent confusion.

NOTE:

A pgBackRest package might install logrotate configuration, such as /etc/logrotate.d/pgbackrest, with a su directive like su postgres postgres. Files in /var/log/pgbackrest belong to the user running pgBackRest, here pgbackrest. Update su to that user. Otherwise, logrotate fails with a permission error.

repository ⇒ Create pgbackrest user

sudo groupadd pgbackrest
sudo adduser -gpgbackrest -n pgbackrest

Prefer package installation to a source build. Packages usually perform the remaining steps in this section. If a package omits a directory or sets incorrect permissions, create the directory or correct its permissions manually.

RHEL packages for pgBackRest are available at yum.postgresql.org.

If your distribution or version has no package, build from source and follow these manual installation steps.

repository ⇒ Install dependencies

sudo yum install postgresql-libs libssh2

repository ⇒ Copy pgBackRest binary from build host

sudo scp build:/build/pgbackrest/src/pgbackrest /usr/bin
sudo chmod 755 /usr/bin/pgbackrest

pgBackRest requires log and configuration directories and a configuration file.

repository ⇒ Create pgBackRest configuration file and directories

sudo mkdir -p -m 770 /var/log/pgbackrest
sudo chown pgbackrest:pgbackrest /var/log/pgbackrest
sudo mkdir -p /etc/pgbackrest
sudo mkdir -p /etc/pgbackrest/conf.d
sudo touch /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf
sudo chmod 640 /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf
sudo chown pgbackrest:pgbackrest /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf

repository ⇒ Create the pgBackRest repository

sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/pgbackrest
sudo chmod 750 /var/lib/pgbackrest
sudo chown pgbackrest:pgbackrest /var/lib/pgbackrest

Configuration

Use TLS and client certificates for communication between hosts. SSH is also supported; see Setup SSH.

Generate pgBackRest client and server certificates as you would for PostgreSQL. See Secure TCP/IP Connections with TLS.

On the repository host, configure the pg-primary host, user, and database path. Use pg1 for the primary so you can add a standby later.

repository:/etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf ⇒ Configure pg1-host/pg1-host-user and pg1-path

[demo]
pg1-host=pg-primary
pg1-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
pg1-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt
pg1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
pg1-host-type=tls
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data
[global]
repo1-path=/var/lib/pgbackrest
repo1-retention-full=2
start-fast=y
tls-server-address=*
tls-server-auth=pgbackrest-client=*
tls-server-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
tls-server-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.crt
tls-server-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.key

On the database host, configure the repository host and user. repo1-host-user defaults to pgbackrest. If postgres performs restores on the repository host, preferably prevent it from also performing backups. It can read the repository directly if it belongs to the pgbackrest group.

pg-primary:/etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf ⇒ Configure repo1-host/repo1-host-user

[demo]
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data
[global]
log-level-file=detail
repo1-host=repository
repo1-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
repo1-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt
repo1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
repo1-host-type=tls
tls-server-address=*
tls-server-auth=pgbackrest-client=demo
tls-server-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
tls-server-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.crt
tls-server-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.key

See Configure Archiving for PostgreSQL configuration.

Commands work as in a single-host setup. However, run commands such as backup and expire on the repository host.

Setup TLS Server

The pgBackRest TLS server must be configured and started on each host.

repository ⇒ Setup pgBackRest Server

sudo cat /etc/systemd/system/pgbackrest.service
[Unit]
Description=pgBackRest Server
After=network.target
StartLimitIntervalSec=0
[Service]
Type=notify
Restart=always
RestartSec=1
User=pgbackrest
ExecStart=/usr/bin/pgbackrest server
ExecStartPost=/bin/sleep 3
ExecStartPost=/bin/bash -c "[ ! -z $MAINPID ]"
ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
sudo systemctl enable pgbackrest
sudo systemctl start pgbackrest

pg-primary ⇒ Setup pgBackRest Server

sudo cat /etc/systemd/system/pgbackrest.service
[Unit]
Description=pgBackRest Server
After=network.target
StartLimitIntervalSec=0
[Service]
Type=notify
Restart=always
RestartSec=1
User=postgres
ExecStart=/usr/bin/pgbackrest server
ExecStartPost=/bin/sleep 3
ExecStartPost=/bin/bash -c "[ ! -z $MAINPID ]"
ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
sudo systemctl enable pgbackrest
sudo systemctl start pgbackrest

Create and Check Stanza

Create the stanza in the new repository.

repository ⇒ Create the stanza

sudo -u pgbackrest pgbackrest --stanza=demo stanza-create

Check configuration on both the database and repository hosts. See Check the Configuration for check details.

pg-primary ⇒ Check the configuration

sudo -u postgres pgbackrest --stanza=demo check

repository ⇒ Check the configuration

sudo -u pgbackrest pgbackrest --stanza=demo check

Perform a Backup

On the repository host, run pgBackRest backup to back up the PostgreSQL cluster.

repository ⇒ Backup the demo cluster

sudo -u pgbackrest pgbackrest --stanza=demo backup
P00   WARN: no prior backup exists, incr backup has been changed to full

The new repository had no full backup. pgBackRest therefore warned that it changed the incremental backup to a full backup.

Restore a Backup

On the database host, run pgBackRest restore to restore the PostgreSQL cluster.

pg-primary ⇒ Stop the demo cluster, restore, and restart PostgreSQL

sudo systemctl stop postgresql-14.service
sudo -u postgres pgbackrest --stanza=demo --delta restore
sudo systemctl start postgresql-14.service

Parallel Backup / Restore

pgBackRest can compress and transfer data in parallel. Set the process count with --process-max.

Usually, allocate no more than 25% of available CPUs to backup. Regular backups do not need maximum speed. Avoid reducing database performance where possible.

Restore should use all available CPUs because PostgreSQL is stopped and usually no other critical work runs on that host. If the host has multiple clusters, account for them when setting parallelism.

repository ⇒ Perform a backup with single process

sudo -u pgbackrest pgbackrest --stanza=demo --type=full backup

repository:/etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf ⇒ Configure pgBackRest to use multiple backup processes

[demo]
pg1-host=pg-primary
pg1-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
pg1-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt
pg1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
pg1-host-type=tls
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data
[global]
process-max=3
repo1-path=/var/lib/pgbackrest
repo1-retention-full=2
start-fast=y
tls-server-address=*
tls-server-auth=pgbackrest-client=*
tls-server-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
tls-server-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.crt
tls-server-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.key

repository ⇒ Perform a backup with multiple processes

sudo -u pgbackrest pgbackrest --stanza=demo --type=full backup

repository ⇒ Get backup info for the demo cluster

sudo -u pgbackrest pgbackrest info
stanza: demo
    status: ok
    cipher: none

    db (current)
        wal archive min/max (14): 000000070000000000000023/000000070000000000000025

        full backup: 20260927-101240F
            timestamp start/stop: 2026-09-27 10:12:40+00 / 2026-09-27 10:12:44+00

            wal start/stop: 000000070000000000000023 / 000000070000000000000023
            database size: 33.5MB, database backup size: 33.5MB
            repo1: backup set size: 4.2MB, backup size: 4.2MB

        full backup: 20260927-101245F
            timestamp start/stop: 2026-09-27 10:12:45+00 / 2026-09-27 10:12:47+00

            wal start/stop: 000000070000000000000024 / 000000070000000000000025
            database size: 33.5MB, database backup size: 33.5MB
            repo1: backup set size: 4.2MB, backup size: 4.2MB

Multiple processes should speed up the last backup. For very small backups, the difference might be small. Time savings increase with database size.

Starting and Stopping

Prevent test clusters from writing to pgBackRest repositories with stop. This includes standbys promoted for testing and test clusters restored from production backups.

stop blocks these write commands: archive-push, backup, expire, stanza-create, and stanza-upgrade. The exception is stanza-delete; see Delete a Stanza.

pg-primary ⇒ Stop pgBackRest write commands

sudo -u postgres pgbackrest stop

New pgBackRest write commands cannot run.

repository ⇒ Attempt a backup

sudo -u pgbackrest pgbackrest --stanza=demo backup
P00   WARN: unable to check pg1: [StopError] raised from remote-0 tls protocol on 'pg-primary': stop file exists for all stanzas

P00  ERROR: [056]: unable to find primary cluster - cannot proceed
            HINT: are all available clusters in recovery?

Use --force to terminate running pgBackRest write commands. This also terminates asynchronous archive-get, although it restarts if PostgreSQL needs it. Repeating stop when pgBackRest is already stopped produces a warning.

pg-primary ⇒ Stop the pgBackRest services again

sudo -u postgres pgbackrest stop
P00   WARN: stop file already exists for all stanzas

Use start to permit pgBackRest write commands again. Previously interrupted commands do not restart automatically.

pg-primary ⇒ Start pgBackRest write commands

sudo -u postgres pgbackrest start

You can also stop pgBackRest for one stanza.

pg-primary ⇒ Stop pgBackRest write commands for the demo stanza

sudo -u postgres pgbackrest --stanza=demo stop

New pgBackRest write commands cannot run for this stanza.

repository ⇒ Attempt a backup

sudo -u pgbackrest pgbackrest --stanza=demo backup
P00   WARN: unable to check pg1: [StopError] raised from remote-0 tls protocol on 'pg-primary': stop file exists for stanza demo

P00  ERROR: [056]: unable to find primary cluster - cannot proceed
            HINT: are all available clusters in recovery?

When starting write commands for one stanza, specify that stanza again.

pg-primary ⇒ Start pgBackRest write commands for the demo stanza

sudo -u postgres pgbackrest --stanza=demo start

Replication

Replication creates standby copies of a PostgreSQL primary cluster. Standbys distribute read load and provide redundancy if the primary host fails.

Installation

Create a host named pg-standby for the standby.

Prefer package installation to a source build. Packages usually perform the remaining steps in this section. If a package omits a directory or sets incorrect permissions, create the directory or correct its permissions manually.

RHEL packages for pgBackRest are available at yum.postgresql.org.

If your distribution or version has no package, build from source and follow these manual installation steps.

pg-standby ⇒ Install dependencies

sudo yum install postgresql-libs libssh2

pg-standby ⇒ Copy pgBackRest binary from build host

sudo scp build:/build/pgbackrest/src/pgbackrest /usr/bin
sudo chmod 755 /usr/bin/pgbackrest

pgBackRest requires log and configuration directories and a configuration file.

pg-standby ⇒ Create pgBackRest configuration file and directories

sudo mkdir -p -m 770 /var/log/pgbackrest
sudo chown postgres:postgres /var/log/pgbackrest
sudo mkdir -p /etc/pgbackrest
sudo mkdir -p /etc/pgbackrest/conf.d
sudo touch /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf
sudo chmod 640 /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf
sudo chown postgres:postgres /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf

Hot Standby

A hot standby performs replication using the WAL archive and allows read-only queries.

Use configuration similar to pg-primary. Set recovery type standby to keep the cluster in recovery after it reaches the end of archived WAL.

pg-standby:/etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf ⇒ Configure pgBackRest on the standby

[demo]
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data
[global]
log-level-file=detail
repo1-host=repository
repo1-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
repo1-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt
repo1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
repo1-host-type=tls
tls-server-address=*
tls-server-auth=pgbackrest-client=demo
tls-server-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
tls-server-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.crt
tls-server-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.key

pg-standby ⇒ Setup pgBackRest Server

sudo cat /etc/systemd/system/pgbackrest.service
[Unit]
Description=pgBackRest Server
After=network.target
StartLimitIntervalSec=0
[Service]
Type=notify
Restart=always
RestartSec=1
User=postgres
ExecStart=/usr/bin/pgbackrest server
ExecStartPost=/bin/sleep 3
ExecStartPost=/bin/bash -c "[ ! -z $MAINPID ]"
ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
sudo systemctl enable pgbackrest
sudo systemctl start pgbackrest

Create the path where PostgreSQL will be restored.

pg-standby ⇒ Create PostgreSQL path

sudo -u postgres mkdir -p -m 700 /var/lib/pgsql/14/data

Create the standby with restore.

IMPORTANT:

If promotion is for testing or reporting rather than a new primary, disable archiving. Use --archive-mode=off or set archive_mode=off in postgresql.conf. Otherwise, the cluster can add conflicting WAL to the repository and complicate restores.

pg-standby ⇒ Restore the demo standby cluster

sudo -u postgres pgbackrest --stanza=demo --type=standby restore
sudo -u postgres cat /var/lib/pgsql/14/data/postgresql.auto.conf

# Do not edit this file manually!
# It will be overwritten by the ALTER SYSTEM command.

# Recovery settings generated by pgBackRest restore on 2026-09-27 10:10:05
restore_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=demo archive-get %f "%p"'

# Recovery settings generated by pgBackRest restore on 2026-09-27 10:10:28
restore_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=demo archive-get %f "%p"'

# Recovery settings generated by pgBackRest restore on 2026-09-27 10:10:53
restore_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=demo archive-get %f "%p"'

This configuration also supports later promotion of the standby to primary.

pg-standby:/var/lib/pgsql/14/data/postgresql.conf ⇒ Configure PostgreSQL

archive_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=demo archive-push %p'
archive_mode = on

log_filename = 'postgresql.log'

pg-standby ⇒ Start PostgreSQL

sudo systemctl start postgresql-14.service

Check the PostgreSQL recovery log. It should show that the cluster entered standby mode and accepts read-only connections.

pg-standby ⇒ Examine the PostgreSQL log output for log messages indicating success

sudo -u postgres cat /var/lib/pgsql/14/data/log/postgresql.log
       [filtered 4 lines of output]
LOG:  listening on Unix socket "/tmp/.s.PGSQL.5432"
LOG:  database system was interrupted; last known up at 2026-09-27 10:12:45 UTC

LOG:  entering standby mode

LOG:  restored log file "00000007.history" from archive
LOG:  restored log file "000000070000000000000024" from archive
       [filtered 3 lines of output]

To test replication, create a table on pg-primary.

pg-primary ⇒ Create a new table on the primary

sudo -u postgres psql -c " \
       begin; \
       create table replicated_table (message text); \
       insert into replicated_table values ('Important Data'); \
       commit; \
       select * from replicated_table";
       [filtered 4 lines of output]
    message
----------------

 Important Data

(1 row)

Then query that table on pg-standby.

pg-standby ⇒ Query new table on the standby

sudo -u postgres psql -c "select * from replicated_table;"
ERROR:  relation "replicated_table" does not exist

LINE 1: select * from replicated_table;
                      ^

The standby reads archived WAL. It cannot see changes until pg-primary archives the segment containing them.

Call pg_switch_wal() to archive the current WAL segment. PostgreSQL creates a new segment for later changes.

pg-primary ⇒ Call pg_switch_wal()

sudo -u postgres psql -c "select *, current_timestamp from pg_switch_wal()";
 pg_switch_wal |      current_timestamp
---------------+------------------------------
 0/2601E7C0    | 2026-09-27 10:13:14.65946+00
(1 row)

After a short delay, the table appears on pg-standby.

pg-standby ⇒ Now the new table exists on the standby (may require a few retries)

sudo -u postgres psql -c " \
       select *, current_timestamp from replicated_table"
    message     |       current_timestamp
----------------+-------------------------------
 Important Data | 2026-09-27 10:13:15.866308+00

(1 row)

Check the standby configuration for access to the repository.

pg-standby ⇒ Check the configuration

sudo -u postgres pgbackrest --stanza=demo --log-level-console=info check

Streaming Replication

Streaming replication connects directly to the primary and applies changes as they occur. This reduces primary-to-standby lag compared with archive-only replication.

Streaming replication requires a user with the replication privilege.

pg-primary ⇒ Create replication user

sudo -u postgres psql -c " \
       create user replicator password 'jw8s0F4' replication";
CREATE ROLE

Update pg_hba.conf to allow the standby to connect as the replication user. Replace the example IP address with your pg-standby address. Reload configuration after the change.

pg-primary ⇒ Create pg_hba.conf entry for replication user

sudo -u postgres sh -c 'echo \
       "host    replication     replicator      172.17.0.8/32           md5" \
       >> /var/lib/pgsql/14/data/pg_hba.conf'

sudo systemctl reload postgresql-14.service

Configure primary_conninfo in pgBackRest so the standby can contact the primary.

pg-standby:/etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf ⇒ Set primary_conninfo

[demo]
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data
recovery-option=primary_conninfo=host=172.17.0.6 port=5432 user=replicator
[global]
log-level-file=detail
repo1-host=repository
repo1-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
repo1-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt
repo1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
repo1-host-type=tls
tls-server-address=*
tls-server-auth=pgbackrest-client=demo
tls-server-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
tls-server-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.crt
tls-server-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.key

You can put a password in primary_conninfo, but a .pgpass file is more flexible and secure.

pg-standby ⇒ Configure the replication password in the .pgpass file.

sudo -u postgres sh -c 'echo \
       "172.17.0.6:*:replication:replicator:jw8s0F4" \
       >> /var/lib/pgsql/.pgpass'

sudo -u postgres chmod 600 /var/lib/pgsql/.pgpass

Create the standby with restore.

pg-standby ⇒ Stop PostgreSQL and restore the demo standby cluster

sudo systemctl stop postgresql-14.service
sudo -u postgres pgbackrest --stanza=demo --delta --type=standby restore
sudo -u postgres cat /var/lib/pgsql/14/data/postgresql.auto.conf

# Do not edit this file manually!
# It will be overwritten by the ALTER SYSTEM command.

# Recovery settings generated by pgBackRest restore on 2026-09-27 10:10:05
restore_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=demo archive-get %f "%p"'

# Recovery settings generated by pgBackRest restore on 2026-09-27 10:10:28
restore_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=demo archive-get %f "%p"'

# Recovery settings generated by pgBackRest restore on 2026-09-27 10:10:53
restore_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=demo archive-get %f "%p"'
# Removed by pgBackRest restore on 2026-09-27 10:11:54 # recovery_target_time = '2026-09-27 10:10:45.829508+00'
# Removed by pgBackRest restore on 2026-09-27 10:11:54 # recovery_target_action = 'promote'

# Recovery settings generated by pgBackRest restore on 2026-09-27 10:11:54
restore_command = 'pgbackrest --repo=3 --repo-target-time="2026-09-27 10:11:38+00" --stanza=demo archive-get %f "%p"'

# Recovery settings generated by pgBackRest restore on 2026-09-27 10:12:36
restore_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=demo archive-get %f "%p"'

# Recovery settings generated by pgBackRest restore on 2026-09-27 10:13:21
primary_conninfo = 'host=172.17.0.6 port=5432 user=replicator'
restore_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=demo archive-get %f "%p"'

NOTE:

pgBackRest wrote primary_conninfo to postgresql.auto.conf because pgbackrest.conf defines it as a recovery-option. To preserve an existing postgresql.auto.conf, run restore with --type=preserve.

RHEL keeps postgresql.conf in the data directory by default. The last restore overwrote its changes, so enable hot_standby again. Alternatively, store postgresql.conf elsewhere or enable hot_standby on pg-primary, where it is ignored.

pg-standby:/var/lib/pgsql/14/data/postgresql.conf ⇒ Enable hot_standby

archive_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=demo archive-push %p'
archive_mode = on
hot_standby = on
log_filename = 'postgresql.log'

pg-standby ⇒ Start PostgreSQL

sudo systemctl start postgresql-14.service

Check the PostgreSQL log to confirm that streaming replication started.

pg-standby ⇒ Examine the PostgreSQL log output for log messages indicating success

sudo -u postgres cat /var/lib/pgsql/14/data/log/postgresql.log
       [filtered 12 lines of output]
LOG:  database system is ready to accept read-only connections
LOG:  restored log file "000000070000000000000026" from archive

LOG:  started streaming WAL from primary at 0/27000000 on timeline 7

New tables on pg-primary now appear quickly on pg-standby without pg_switch_wal().

pg-primary ⇒ Create a new table on the primary

sudo -u postgres psql -c " \
       begin; \
       create table stream_table (message text); \
       insert into stream_table values ('Important Data'); \
       commit; \
       select *, current_timestamp from stream_table";
       [filtered 4 lines of output]
    message     |       current_timestamp
----------------+-------------------------------
 Important Data | 2026-09-27 10:13:26.824575+00

(1 row)

pg-standby ⇒ Query table on the standby

sudo -u postgres psql -c " \

Multiple Stanzas

pgBackRest supports multiple stanzas, commonly with one shared repository host.

Installation

Create a host named pg-alt for the new primary.

Prefer package installation to a source build. Packages usually perform the remaining steps in this section. If a package omits a directory or sets incorrect permissions, create the directory or correct its permissions manually.

RHEL packages for pgBackRest are available at yum.postgresql.org.

If your distribution or version has no package, build from source and follow these manual installation steps.

pg-alt ⇒ Install dependencies

sudo yum install postgresql-libs libssh2

pg-alt ⇒ Copy pgBackRest binary from build host

sudo scp build:/build/pgbackrest/src/pgbackrest /usr/bin
sudo chmod 755 /usr/bin/pgbackrest

pgBackRest requires log and configuration directories and a configuration file.

pg-alt ⇒ Create pgBackRest configuration file and directories

sudo mkdir -p -m 770 /var/log/pgbackrest
sudo chown postgres:postgres /var/log/pgbackrest
sudo mkdir -p /etc/pgbackrest
sudo mkdir -p /etc/pgbackrest/conf.d
sudo touch /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf
sudo chmod 640 /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf
sudo chown postgres:postgres /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf

Configuration

Use configuration similar to pg-primary, but select stanza demo-alt. This separates its backups and archive.

pg-alt:/etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf ⇒ Configure pgBackRest on the new primary

[demo-alt]
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data
[global]
log-level-file=detail
repo1-host=repository
repo1-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
repo1-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt
repo1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
repo1-host-type=tls
tls-server-address=*
tls-server-auth=pgbackrest-client=demo-alt
tls-server-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
tls-server-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.crt
tls-server-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.key

repository:/etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf ⇒ Configure pg1-host/pg1-host-user and pg1-path

[demo]
pg1-host=pg-primary
pg1-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
pg1-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt
pg1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
pg1-host-type=tls
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data
[demo-alt]
pg1-host=pg-alt
pg1-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
pg1-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt
pg1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
pg1-host-type=tls
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data
[global]
process-max=3
repo1-path=/var/lib/pgbackrest
repo1-retention-full=2
start-fast=y
tls-server-address=*
tls-server-auth=pgbackrest-client=*
tls-server-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
tls-server-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.crt
tls-server-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.key

pg-alt ⇒ Setup pgBackRest Server

sudo cat /etc/systemd/system/pgbackrest.service
[Unit]
Description=pgBackRest Server
After=network.target
StartLimitIntervalSec=0
[Service]
Type=notify
Restart=always
RestartSec=1
User=postgres
ExecStart=/usr/bin/pgbackrest server
ExecStartPost=/bin/sleep 3
ExecStartPost=/bin/bash -c "[ ! -z $MAINPID ]"
ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
sudo systemctl enable pgbackrest
sudo systemctl start pgbackrest

Setup Demo Cluster

pg-alt ⇒ Create the demo cluster

sudo -u postgres /usr/pgsql-14/bin/initdb \
       -D /var/lib/pgsql/14/data -k -A peer

pg-alt:/var/lib/pgsql/14/data/postgresql.conf ⇒ Configure PostgreSQL settings

archive_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=demo-alt archive-push %p'
archive_mode = on
log_filename = 'postgresql.log'

pg-alt ⇒ Start the demo cluster

sudo systemctl restart postgresql-14.service

Create the Stanza and Check Configuration

Run stanza-create to initialize the stanza. Then run check to verify archive and backup configuration.

Asynchronous Archiving

Enable archive-async for asynchronous archive-push and archive-get.

Create a spool path for transient data. Each command uses it differently, as described in the following sections.

pg-primary ⇒ Create the spool directory

sudo mkdir -p -m 750 /var/spool/pgbackrest
sudo chown postgres:postgres /var/spool/pgbackrest

pg-standby ⇒ Create the spool directory

sudo mkdir -p -m 750 /var/spool/pgbackrest
sudo chown postgres:postgres /var/spool/pgbackrest

Configure the spool path and enable asynchronous archiving. This reduces remote-storage connections. Set process-max for parallel operations and further performance improvements. Keep it low enough to preserve normal database performance.

pg-primary:/etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf ⇒ Configure the spool path and asynchronous archiving

[demo]
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data
[global]
archive-async=y
log-level-file=detail
repo1-host=repository
repo1-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
repo1-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt
repo1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
repo1-host-type=tls
spool-path=/var/spool/pgbackrest
tls-server-address=*
tls-server-auth=pgbackrest-client=demo
tls-server-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
tls-server-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.crt
tls-server-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.key
[global:archive-get]
process-max=2
[global:archive-push]
process-max=2

pg-standby:/etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf ⇒ Configure the spool path and asynchronous archiving

[demo]
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data
recovery-option=primary_conninfo=host=172.17.0.6 port=5432 user=replicator
[global]
archive-async=y
log-level-file=detail
repo1-host=repository
repo1-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
repo1-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt
repo1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
repo1-host-type=tls
spool-path=/var/spool/pgbackrest
tls-server-address=*
tls-server-auth=pgbackrest-client=demo
tls-server-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
tls-server-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.crt
tls-server-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.key
[global:archive-get]
process-max=2
[global:archive-push]
process-max=2

NOTE:

Set process-max in command-specific sections so it does not affect backup or restore. You can give archive-push and archive-get different values.

For this demonstration, interrupt streaming replication so PostgreSQL must fetch WAL through restore_command.

pg-primary ⇒ Break streaming replication by changing the replication password

sudo -u postgres psql -c "alter user replicator password 'bogus'"
ALTER ROLE

pg-standby ⇒ Restart standby to break connection

sudo systemctl restart postgresql-14.service

Archive Push

Asynchronous archive-push transfers WAL archiving to separate processes to improve throughput. It finds ready segments beyond the one PostgreSQL currently requests through archive_command. It copies WAL directly from pg_xlog/pg_wal to the archive. The archive_command returns success only after the requested segment is safely stored.

The spool path contains current WAL archive status. Status files are usually empty and use little I/O and space, at most a few MB. pgBackRest can recreate all this information. You do not need to preserve the directory when moving the cluster to new hardware.

IMPORTANT:

The original asynchronous implementation copied WAL to the spool directory before compression and transfer. The newer implementation reads WAL directly from pg_xlog. If you used asynchronous archiving in v1.12 or earlier, read the v1.13 release notes carefully before upgrading.

Monitor asynchronous activity in [stanza]-archive-push-async.log. To test it, push several WAL segments quickly.

pg-primary ⇒ Test parallel asynchronous archiving

sudo -u postgres psql -c " \
       select pg_create_restore_point('test async push'); select pg_switch_wal(); \
       select pg_create_restore_point('test async push'); select pg_switch_wal(); \
       select pg_create_restore_point('test async push'); select pg_switch_wal(); \
       select pg_create_restore_point('test async push'); select pg_switch_wal(); \
       select pg_create_restore_point('test async push'); select pg_switch_wal();"

sudo -u postgres pgbackrest --stanza=demo --log-level-console=info check

Archive Get

Asynchronous archive-get keeps a local WAL queue to improve throughput. If a requested segment is absent, it fetches that segment and enough consecutive segments to fill the queue. archive-get-queue-max controls maximum size. When the queue falls below half full, pgBackRest fetches more WAL to refill it.

Asynchronous operation helps most with high WAL volumes or high-latency repository connections, such as S3 and other object stores. For high latency, consider increasing process-max.

Monitor asynchronous activity in [stanza]-archive-get-async.log.

pg-standby ⇒ Check results in the log

sudo -u postgres cat /var/log/pgbackrest/demo-archive-get-async.log

Backup from a Standby

pgBackRest can back up from a standby instead of the primary. Configure pg-standby and enable backup-standby. If several standbys are configured, it uses the first running standby found.

repository:/etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf ⇒ Configure pg2-host/pg2-host-user and pg2-path

[demo]
pg1-host=pg-primary
pg1-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
pg1-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt
pg1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
pg1-host-type=tls
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data
pg2-host=pg-standby
pg2-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
pg2-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt
pg2-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
pg2-host-type=tls
pg2-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data
[demo-alt]
pg1-host=pg-alt
pg1-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
pg1-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt
pg1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
pg1-host-type=tls
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data
[global]
backup-standby=y
process-max=3
repo1-path=/var/lib/pgbackrest
repo1-retention-full=2
start-fast=y
tls-server-address=*
tls-server-auth=pgbackrest-client=*
tls-server-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
tls-server-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.crt
tls-server-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.key

Backup requires both the primary and standby databases. Most files come from the standby to reduce primary load. Configure hosts in any order. pgBackRest detects their roles automatically.

repository ⇒ Backup the demo cluster from pg2

sudo -u pgbackrest pgbackrest --stanza=demo --log-level-console=detail backup
       [filtered 2 lines of output]

This incremental backup copies most files from pg-standby and only a few from pg-primary.

A standby backup is identical to a primary backup. pgBackRest starts and stops the backup on pg-primary. It copies replicated files from pg-standby and the remaining files from pg-primary. Thus, the backup includes primary logs and statistics.

Upgrading PostgreSQL

Immediately after a PostgreSQL major version upgrade, update pg-path in all pgBackRest configurations to the new database location. Then run stanza-upgrade. It upgrades the stanza in every repository configured on the host. If the database is offline, use --no-online.

These steps outline a primary and standby upgrade to demonstrate pgBackRest reconfiguration. They are not a complete PostgreSQL upgrade guide. Take a backup before upgrading.

pg-primary ⇒ Stop old cluster

sudo systemctl stop postgresql-14.service

Stop the old standby cluster. You will restore it from the upgraded cluster.

pg-standby ⇒ Stop old cluster

sudo systemctl stop postgresql-14.service

Create the new cluster and upgrade it.

pg-primary ⇒ Create new cluster and perform the upgrade

sudo -u postgres /usr/pgsql-15/bin/initdb \
       -D /var/lib/pgsql/15/data -k -A peer

sudo -u postgres sh -c 'cd /var/lib/pgsql && \
       /usr/pgsql-15/bin/pg_upgrade \
       --old-bindir=/usr/pgsql-14/bin \
       --new-bindir=/usr/pgsql-15/bin \
       --old-datadir=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data \
       --new-datadir=/var/lib/pgsql/15/data \
       --old-options=" -c config_file=/var/lib/pgsql/14/data/postgresql.conf" \
       --new-options=" -c config_file=/var/lib/pgsql/15/data/postgresql.conf"'
       [filtered 41 lines of output]
Checking for extension updates                              ok

Upgrade Complete

----------------
Optimizer statistics are not transferred by pg_upgrade.
       [filtered 4 lines of output]

Configure the new cluster settings and port.

pg-primary:/var/lib/pgsql/15/data/postgresql.conf ⇒ Configure PostgreSQL

archive_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=demo archive-push %p'
archive_mode = on
log_filename = 'postgresql.log'

Update pgBackRest configuration on every system to use the new cluster.

pg-primary:/etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf ⇒ Upgrade the pg1-path

[demo]
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/15/data
[global]
archive-async=y

repo1-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
repo1-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt
repo1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
repo1-host-type=tls
spool-path=/var/spool/pgbackrest
tls-server-address=*
tls-server-auth=pgbackrest-client=demo
tls-server-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt
tls-server-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.crt
tls-server-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/server.key
[global:archive-get]
process-max=2
[global:archive-push]
process-max=2

pg-standby:/etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf ⇒ Upgrade the pg-path

[demo]
pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/15/data
recovery-option=primary_conninfo=host=172.17.0.6 port=5432 user=replicator
[global]

repo1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key
repo1-host-type=tls

[global:archive-get]

sudo -u postgres pgbackrest --stanza=demo --no-online \
       --log-level-console=info stanza-upgrade
P00   INFO: stanza-upgrade command begin 2.59.2: --exec-id=7457-16565fb6 --log-level-console=info --log-level-file=detail --no-log-timestamp --no-online --pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/15/data --repo1-host=repository --repo1-host-ca-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/ca.crt --repo1-host-cert-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.crt --repo1-host-key-file=/etc/pgbackrest/cert/client.key --repo1-host-type=tls --stanza=demo

pg-primary ⇒ Remove old cluster

pg-standby ⇒ Remove old cluster and create the new cluster

sudo rm -rf /var/lib/pgsql/14/data
sudo -u postgres mkdir -p -m 700 /usr/pgsql-15/bin

repository ⇒ Check configuration

P00   WARN: unable to check pg2: [DbConnectError] raised from remote-0 tls protocol on 'pg-standby': unable to connect to 'dbname='postgres' port=5432': connection to server on socket "/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432" failed: No such file or directory

4 - Command Reference

pgBackRest command reference with all options for backup, restore, archive, and management operations.

Source: https://pgbackrest.org/command.html

Introduction

Commands execute pgBackRest functions. Each command page lists every applicable option, including options shared with other commands. The lists also include options that you can set in pgbackrest.conf.

Use the reset- prefix on the command line to reset a non-boolean option from pgbackrest.conf to its default. For example, use this feature to restore a backup directly on a repository host. Normally, pgBackRest detects the remote database host and reports an error because remote restores are not supported. Add --reset-pg1-host to ignore the remote database host and restore locally. You might also need --pg1-path to select a path other than the database host path.

Use the no- prefix on the command line to set a boolean option to false.

To set an option through an environment variable, add the PGBACKREST_ prefix. Convert the option name to uppercase and replace - with _. For example, pg1-path becomes PGBACKREST_PG1_PATH, and stanza becomes PGBACKREST_STANZA. Use configuration-file values for boolean options, such as PGBACKREST_COMPRESS="n"; reset-* variants are not permitted. For an option that accepts multiple values on the command line or in a configuration file, separate values with colons. For example, use PGBACKREST_DB_INCLUDE="db1:db2".

Command-line options override environment options. Environment options override configuration-file options.

See Configuration Introduction for information about option types.

Commands

CommandSummary
annotateAdd, modify, or remove backup annotations after the backup is created.
archive-getFetch archived WAL segments for restore, PITR, or replica recovery.
archive-pushAccept WAL segments from PostgreSQL and push them to configured repositories.
backupCreate backups to the target repository (defaults to highest priority repository).
checkValidate stanza backup/archive configuration and WAL archiving health.
expireExpire backups and archived WAL based on configured retention policies.
helpShow command and option help at general, command, or option level.
infoDisplay stanza and backup status/metadata in text or JSON format.
repo-getRead repository files (like cat) for administration, investigation, and testing.
repo-lsList repository files/paths (like ls) for administration, investigation, and testing.
restoreRestore from backup (latest by default) with optional point-in-time recovery.
serverRun the pgBackRest TLS server for remote host access without SSH.
server-pingPing a pgBackRest TLS server to verify it is accepting connections.
stanza-createCreate stanza metadata in all configured repositories.
stanza-deletePermanently remove all backups and archives for a stanza.
stanza-upgradeUpgrade stanza metadata after a PostgreSQL major version upgrade.
startRe-allow pgBackRest processes to run after a previous stop.
stopPrevent new pgBackRest processes and optionally force-stop running ones.
verifyVerify that backup and archive data in the repository is valid.
versionDisplay the installed pgBackRest version.

4.1 - Annotate Command (annotate)

Reference for pgBackRest annotate command options and behavior.

Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: annotate

Use annotate to add, change, or remove annotations after the backup command creates a backup.

Command Options

Backup Annotation Option (--annotation)

Annotate backup with user-defined key/value pairs.

Attach informative key/value pairs to the backup. Repeat this option to attach multiple annotations.

When --set specifies a backup, the info command includes its annotations in text output. JSON output always includes annotations.

example: --annotation=source="Sunday backup for website database"

Set Option (--set)

Backup set to annotate.

The backup set to annotate.

example: --set=20150131-153358F_20150131-153401I

General Options

Allow Run as Root Option (--allow-root)

Allow the command to run as the root user.

By default, only restore can run as root because it manages file ownership. Other commands can create root-owned files, for example in the repository. The PostgreSQL user cannot access these files, which causes later commands to fail.

Enable this option to run another command as root. Preferably, run pgBackRest as the user that owns the repository and PostgreSQL cluster.

default: n
example: --allow-root

Buffer Size Option (--buffer-size)

Buffer size for I/O operations.

Set the buffer size for copy, compression, encryption, and other operations. Options determine the number of buffers. Each operation can also use more memory. For example, gz compression can use an additional 256KiB.

Allowed values are 16KiB, 32KiB, 64KiB, 128KiB, 256KiB, 512KiB, 1MiB, 2MiB, 4MiB, 8MiB, and 16MiB.

default: 1MiB
example: --buffer-size=2MiB

SSH Client Command Option (--cmd-ssh)

SSH client command.

Use this option to select a different SSH client or when the ssh command is not in $PATH.

default: ssh
example: --cmd-ssh=/usr/bin/ssh

Network Compress Level Option (--compress-level-network)

Network compression level.

Set the network compression level when compress-type=none and the command runs on a host other than the repository host. Compression reduces network traffic. When compress-type is not none, pgBackRest ignores compress-level-network and uses compress-level. This prevents compression of the same file twice.

default: 1
allowed: [-5, 12]
example: --compress-level-network=1

Config Option (--config)

pgBackRest configuration file.

Use this option to select a configuration file other than the default.

default: CFGOPTDEF_CONFIG_PATH "/" PROJECT_CONFIG_FILE
example: --config=/conf/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf

Config Include Path Option (--config-include-path)

Path to additional pgBackRest configuration files.

pgBackRest combines files with the .conf extension in this location with its configuration file. The result is one configuration file.

default: CFGOPTDEF_CONFIG_PATH "/" PROJECT_CONFIG_INCLUDE_PATH
example: --config-include-path=/conf/pgbackrest/conf.d

Config Path Option (--config-path)

Base path of pgBackRest configuration files.

Set the default base path for --config and --config-include-path. Explicit command-line values for these options override this setting.

For example, specify only --config-path=/conf/pgbackrest to set the --config default to /conf/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf. This also sets the --config-include-path default to /conf/pgbackrest/conf.d.

default: CFGOPTDEF_CONFIG_PATH
example: --config-path=/conf/pgbackrest

I/O Timeout Option (--io-timeout)

I/O timeout.

Set the connection and read/write timeout in seconds.

The complete read/write operation can take longer than this timeout. However, it must make some progress before the timeout, even if only one byte.

default: 1m
allowed: [100ms, 1h]
example: --io-timeout=120

Lock Path Option (--lock-path)

Path where lock files are stored.

pgBackRest creates lock files in this path to prevent conflicting operations from running at the same time.

default: /tmp/pgbackrest
example: --lock-path=/backup/db/lock

Neutral Umask Option (--neutral-umask)

Use a neutral umask.

Set the umask to 0000 to control repository permissions. The default directory mode is 0750. The default file mode is 0640.

To use the executing user’s umask, set neutral-umask=n in the configuration file or --no-neutral-umask on the command line.

default: y
example: --no-neutral-umask

Set Process Priority Option (--priority)

Set process priority.

Set the process priority, or niceness, used by the kernel scheduler. Positive values decrease priority. Negative values increase priority. Processes usually lack permission to increase their priority.

allowed: [-20, 19]
example: --priority=19

Protocol Timeout Option (--protocol-timeout)

Protocol timeout.

Set how many seconds a local or remote process waits for a new protocol message. This prevents an indefinite wait.

NOTE: The protocol-timeout option must be greater than the db-timeout option.

default: 31m
allowed: [100ms, 7d]
example: --protocol-timeout=630

Keep Alive Option (--sck-keep-alive)

Keep-alive enable.

Enables keep-alive messages on socket connections.

default: y
example: --no-sck-keep-alive

Stanza Option (--stanza)

Defines the stanza.

A stanza contains the configuration for a PostgreSQL database cluster. It defines the cluster location, backup method, archive options, and other settings. Most database servers have one PostgreSQL cluster and one stanza. A backup server has a stanza for each cluster that needs a backup.

Choose a stanza name that describes the databases in the cluster. The primary and all replicas use the same stanza name. A functional name, such as app or dw, is preferable to a local cluster name, such as main or prod.

example: --stanza=main

Keep Alive Count Option (--tcp-keep-alive-count)

Keep-alive count.

Set how many TCP keep-alive messages can be lost before the connection is considered dead.

This option is available on systems that support the TCP_KEEPCNT socket option.

allowed: [1, 32]
example: --tcp-keep-alive-count=3

Keep Alive Idle Option (--tcp-keep-alive-idle)

Keep-alive idle time.

Set how many seconds of network inactivity must pass before the operating system sends a TCP keep-alive message.

This option is available on systems that support the TCP_KEEPIDLE socket option.

allowed: [1, 3600]
example: --tcp-keep-alive-idle=60

Keep Alive Interval Option (--tcp-keep-alive-interval)

Keep-alive interval time.

Set how many seconds to wait before retransmitting a TCP keep-alive message that has no acknowledgement.

This option is available on systems that support the TCP_KEEPINTVL socket option.

allowed: [1, 900]
example: --tcp-keep-alive-interval=30

TLSv1.2 cipher suites Option (--tls-cipher-12)

Allowed TLSv1.2 cipher suites.

All TLS connections between the pgBackRest client and server use encryption. Connections to object stores, such as S3, also use encryption by default.

NOTE: The absolute minimum security level for any transport connection is TLSv1.2.

Change the accepted cipher suites if necessary. The example is suitable unless you have specific security requirements. By default, this option is unset and the underlying OpenSSL library default applies.

example: --tls-cipher-12=HIGH:MEDIUM:+3DES:!aNULL

TLSv1.3 cipher suites Option (--tls-cipher-13)

Allowed TLSv1.3 cipher suites.

All TLS connections between the pgBackRest client and server use encryption. Connections to object stores, such as S3, also use encryption by default.

NOTE: The absolute minimum security level for any transport connection is TLSv1.2.

Change the accepted cipher suites if necessary. By default, this option is unset and the underlying OpenSSL library default applies.

example: --tls-cipher-13=TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256

Log Options

Console Log Level Option (--log-level-console)

Level for console logging.

The following log levels are supported:

  • off - No logging at all (not recommended)
  • error - Log only errors
  • warn - Log warnings and errors
  • info - Log info, warnings, and errors
  • detail - Log detail, info, warnings, and errors
  • debug - Log debug, detail, info, warnings, and errors
  • trace - Log trace (very verbose debugging), debug, info, warnings, and errors
default: warn
example: --log-level-console=error

File Log Level Option (--log-level-file)

Level for file logging.

The following log levels are supported:

  • off - No logging at all (not recommended)
  • error - Log only errors
  • warn - Log warnings and errors
  • info - Log info, warnings, and errors
  • detail - Log detail, info, warnings, and errors
  • debug - Log debug, detail, info, warnings, and errors
  • trace - Log trace (very verbose debugging), debug, info, warnings, and errors
default: info
example: --log-level-file=debug

Std Error Log Level Option (--log-level-stderr)

Level for stderr logging.

Select the log levels that write to stderr instead of stdout, which log-level-console controls. Output to stderr excludes the timestamp and process.

The following log levels are supported:

  • off - No logging at all (not recommended)
  • error - Log only errors
  • warn - Log warnings and errors
  • info - Log info, warnings, and errors
  • detail - Log detail, info, warnings, and errors
  • debug - Log debug, detail, info, warnings, and errors
  • trace - Log trace (very verbose debugging), debug, info, warnings, and errors
default: off
example: --log-level-stderr=error

Log Path Option (--log-path)

Path where log files are stored.

pgBackRest stores log files in this path. If log-level-file=off, no log path is necessary.

default: /var/log/pgbackrest
example: --log-path=/backup/db/log

Log Subprocesses Option (--log-subprocess)

Enable logging in subprocesses.

Enable file logging for subprocesses created by this process. Use the level specified by log-level-file.

default: n
example: --log-subprocess

Log Timestamp Option (--log-timestamp)

Enable timestamp in logging.

Include timestamps in console and file logs. Disable this option for special uses, such as documentation generation.

default: y
example: --no-log-timestamp

Repository Options

Set Repository Option (--repo)

Set repository.

Set the repository for a command to operate on.

For example, select a repository for a restore instead of letting pgBackRest choose one.

allowed: [1, 256]
example: --repo=1

Azure Repository Container Option (--repo-azure-container)

Azure repository container.

Azure container used to store the repository.

Set repo-path=/ to store the repository in the container root. Usually, specify a prefix such as /repo. The container can then also store logs and other Azure-generated content.

example: --repo1-azure-container=pg-backup

Azure Repository Key Type Option (--repo-azure-key-type)

Azure repository key type.

The following types are supported for authorization:

  • shared - Shared key
  • sas - Shared access signature
  • auto - Automatically authorize using Azure managed identities
default: shared
example: --repo1-azure-key-type=sas

Azure Repository URI Style Option (--repo-azure-uri-style)

Azure URI Style.

The following URI styles are supported:

  • host - Connect to account.endpoint host.
  • path - Connect to endpoint host and prepend account to URIs.
default: host
example: --repo1-azure-uri-style=path

Repository Cipher Type Option (--repo-cipher-type)

Cipher used to encrypt the repository.

The following cipher types are supported:

  • none - The repository is not encrypted
  • aes-256-cbc - Advanced Encryption Standard with 256 bit key length

pgBackRest always encrypts data on the client, even when the repository type, such as S3, supports encryption.

default: none
example: --repo1-cipher-type=aes-256-cbc

GCS Repository Bucket Option (--repo-gcs-bucket)

GCS repository bucket.

GCS bucket used to store the repository.

Set repo-path=/ to store the repository in the bucket root. Usually, specify a prefix such as /repo. The bucket can then also store logs and other GCS-generated content.

example: --repo1-gcs-bucket=/pg-backup

GCS Repository Endpoint Option (--repo-gcs-endpoint)

GCS repository endpoint.

Set the endpoint for the storage service connection. You can select a local GCS server or another endpoint.

default: storage.googleapis.com
example: --repo1-gcs-endpoint=localhost

GCS Repository Key Type Option (--repo-gcs-key-type)

GCS repository key type.

The following types are supported for authorization:

  • auto - Authorize using the instance service account.
  • service - Service account from locally stored key.
  • token - For local testing, e.g. fakegcs.

When repo-gcs-key-type=service, pgBackRest reloads credentials when it renews the authentication token.

default: service
example: --repo1-gcs-key-type=auto

GCS Repository Project ID Option (--repo-gcs-user-project)

GCS project ID.

GCS project ID used to determine request billing.

example: --repo1-gcs-user-project=my-project

Repository Host Option (--repo-host)

Repository host when operating remotely.

This setting is not necessary for backups and archives on a locally mounted filesystem.

example: --repo1-host=repo1.domain.com

Deprecated Name: backup-host

Repository Host Certificate Authority File Option (--repo-host-ca-file)

Repository host certificate authority file.

Use a CA file other than the system default for connecting to the repository host.

example: --repo1-host-ca-file=/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt

Repository Host Certificate Authority Path Option (--repo-host-ca-path)

Repository host certificate authority path.

Use a CA path other than the system default for connecting to the repository host.

example: --repo1-host-ca-path=/etc/pki/tls/certs

Repository Host Certificate File Option (--repo-host-cert-file)

Repository host certificate file.

pgBackRest sends this certificate to the repository host to prove the client identity.

example: --repo1-host-cert-file=/path/to/client.crt

Repository Host Command Option (--repo-host-cmd)

Repository host pgBackRest command.

Set this option only when the pgBackRest command path differs between the local and repository hosts. Otherwise, the repository host uses the local command path.

default: [path of executed pgbackrest binary]
example: --repo1-host-cmd=/usr/lib/backrest/bin/pgbackrest

Deprecated Name: backup-cmd

Repository Host Configuration Option (--repo-host-config)

pgBackRest repository host configuration file.

Set the repository host configuration file location. This is necessary only when it differs from the local configuration file location.

default: CFGOPTDEF_CONFIG_PATH "/" PROJECT_CONFIG_FILE
example: --repo1-host-config=/conf/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf

Deprecated Name: backup-config

Repository Host Configuration Include Path Option (--repo-host-config-include-path)

pgBackRest repository host configuration include path.

Set the repository host configuration include path. This is necessary only when it differs from the local configuration include path.

default: CFGOPTDEF_CONFIG_PATH "/" PROJECT_CONFIG_INCLUDE_PATH
example: --repo1-host-config-include-path=/conf/pgbackrest/conf.d

Repository Host Configuration Path Option (--repo-host-config-path)

pgBackRest repository host configuration path.

Set the repository host configuration path. This is necessary only when it differs from the local configuration path.

default: CFGOPTDEF_CONFIG_PATH
example: --repo1-host-config-path=/conf/pgbackrest

Repository Host Key File Option (--repo-host-key-file)

Repository host key file.

This key proves that the certificate owner sent the client certificate.

example: --repo1-host-key-file=/path/to/client.key

Repository Host Port Option (--repo-host-port)

Repository host port when repo-host is set.

Use this option to specify a non-default port for the repository host protocol.

NOTE: When repo-host-type=ssh, repo-host-port has no default. The command specified by cmd-ssh supplies its configured port.

default (depending on repo-host-type):
    tls - 8432

allowed: [0, 65535]
example: --repo1-host-port=25

Deprecated Name: backup-ssh-port

Repository Host Protocol Type Option (--repo-host-type)

Repository host protocol type.

The following protocol types are supported:

  • ssh - Secure Shell.
  • tls - pgBackRest TLS server.
default: ssh
example: --repo1-host-type=tls

Repository Host User Option (--repo-host-user)

Repository host user when repo-host is set.

Set the user for repository host operations. Prefer a separate user, such as pgbackrest, to the postgres user. If PostgreSQL runs on the repository host, you can add postgres to the pgbackrest group. This gives it read access to the repository without permission to damage its contents accidentally.

default: pgbackrest
example: --repo1-host-user=repo-user

Deprecated Name: backup-user

Repository Path Option (--repo-path)

Path where backups and archive are stored.

The repository is where pgBackRest stores backups and archives WAL segments.

To estimate repository space, take some backups. Record the sizes of full, incremental, and differential backups (full/incr/diff). Measure how much WAL the database generates each day. These measurements give an approximate space requirement. Requirements will probably change as the database changes.

default: /var/lib/pgbackrest
example: --repo1-path=/backup/db/backrest

S3 Repository Bucket Option (--repo-s3-bucket)

S3 repository bucket.

S3 bucket used to store the repository.

Set repo-path=/ to store the repository in the bucket root. Usually, specify a prefix such as /repo. The bucket can then also store logs and other AWS-generated content.

example: --repo1-s3-bucket=pg-backup

S3 Repository Endpoint Option (--repo-s3-endpoint)

S3 repository endpoint.

The AWS endpoint should be valid for the selected region.

For custom/test configurations the repo-storage-ca-file, repo-storage-ca-path, repo-storage-host, repo-storage-port, and repo-storage-verify-tls options may be useful.

example: --repo1-s3-endpoint=s3.amazonaws.com

S3 Repository Key Type Option (--repo-s3-key-type)

S3 repository key type.

The following types are supported:

  • shared - Shared keys
  • auto - Automatically retrieve temporary credentials
  • web-id - Automatically retrieve web identity credentials
  • pod-id - Automatically retrieve EKS pod identity credentials
  • process - Retrieve credentials by executing a process
default: shared
example: --repo1-s3-key-type=auto

S3 Repository KMS Key ID Option (--repo-s3-kms-key-id)

S3 repository KMS key.

Enables S3 server-side encryption using the specified AWS key management service key.

example: --repo1-s3-kms-key-id=bceb4f13-6939-4be3-910d-df54dee817b7

S3 Authentication Process Command Option (--repo-s3-process-cmd)

S3 authentication process command.

Set the command and optional arguments that retrieve temporary S3 credentials. The first list entry is the command. The remaining entries are its parameters.

The process must output JSON with AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, SessionToken, and Expiration fields. pgBackRest refreshes credentials automatically before they expire. See Process Credential Provider for the format.

example: --repo1-s3-process-cmd=/usr/local/bin/get-credentials --repo1-s3-process-cmd=--role --repo1-s3-process-cmd=my-role

S3 Repository Region Option (--repo-s3-region)

S3 repository region.

The AWS region where the bucket was created.

example: --repo1-s3-region=us-east-1

S3 Repository Requestor Pays Option (--repo-s3-requester-pays)

S3 repository requester pays.

Enables S3 requester pays.

default: n
example: --no-repo1-s3-requester-pays

S3 Repository Role Option (--repo-s3-role)

S3 repository role.

When repo-s3-key-type=auto, set the AWS role name used to retrieve temporary credentials. Use the name, not the full ARN.

example: --repo1-s3-role=authrole

S3 Repository Service Option (--repo-s3-service)

S3 signing service.

Set the signing service for SigV4 authentication. The default is s3 for standard S3 endpoints. For an S3 Outposts endpoint, use s3-outposts.

default: s3
example: --repo1-s3-service=s3-outposts

S3 Repository STS Endpoint Option (--repo-s3-sts-host)

S3 repository STS endpoint.

When repo-s3-key-type=web-id, this endpoint retrieves temporary credentials. To use regional STS, select a regional endpoint, such as sts.us-east-1.amazonaws.com. Regional STS might be necessary for GovCloud or China regions, or to reduce latency.

default: sts.amazonaws.com
example: --repo1-s3-sts-host=sts.us-east-1.amazonaws.com

S3 Repository URI Style Option (--repo-s3-uri-style)

S3 URI Style.

The following URI styles are supported:

  • host - Connect to bucket.endpoint host.
  • path - Connect to endpoint host and prepend bucket to URIs.
default: host
example: --repo1-s3-uri-style=path

SFTP Repository Host Option (--repo-sftp-host)

SFTP repository host.

The SFTP host containing the repository.

example: --repo1-sftp-host=sftprepo.domain

SFTP Repository Host Fingerprint Option (--repo-sftp-host-fingerprint)

SFTP repository host fingerprint.

Generate the SFTP host fingerprint with the hash type specified by repo-sftp-host-key-hash-type. Use awk '{print $2}' ssh_host_xxx_key.pub | base64 -d | (md5sum or sha1sum) -b. SSH host keys are usually in /etc/ssh.

example: --repo1-sftp-host-fingerprint=f84e172dfead7aeeeae6c1fdfb5aa8cf

SFTP Host Key Check Type Option (--repo-sftp-host-key-check-type)

SFTP host key check type.

The following SFTP host key check types are supported:

  • strict - pgBackRest never adds host keys to ~/.ssh/known_hosts automatically. It refuses connections when a host key changes or is absent from the known hosts files. Add each new host manually.
  • accept-new - pgBackRest automatically adds new host keys to the user’s known hosts file. It refuses connections when a host key changes.
  • fingerprint - pgBackRest compares the host key with the repo-sftp-host-fingerprint value.
  • none - pgBackRest does not check host keys.
default: strict
example: --repo1-sftp-host-key-check-type=accept-new

SFTP Repository Host Key Hash Type Option (--repo-sftp-host-key-hash-type)

SFTP repository host key hash type.

Set the hash type used to calculate the remote host key digest at SSH startup. Newer libssh2 versions support sha256 as well as md5 and sha1.

example: --repo1-sftp-host-key-hash-type=sha256

SFTP Repository Host Port Option (--repo-sftp-host-port)

SFTP repository host port.

SFTP repository host port.

default: 22
allowed: [1, 65535]
example: --repo1-sftp-host-port=22

SFTP Repository Host User Option (--repo-sftp-host-user)

SFTP repository host user.

User on the host used to store the repository.

example: --repo1-sftp-host-user=pg-backup

SFTP Known Hosts File Option (--repo-sftp-known-host)

SFTP known hosts file.

Set a known hosts file to check during SFTP authentication. By default, pgBackRest searches ~/.ssh/known_hosts, ~/.ssh/known_hosts2, /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts, and /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts2. If you configure file paths, it searches those files. Use absolute paths or paths that start with a tilde. Repeat repo-sftp-known-host to specify multiple files. To check known hosts files, do not set repo-sftp-host-fingerprint.

See also the repo-sftp-host-check-type option.

example: --repo1-sftp-known-host=/home/postgres/.ssh/known_hosts

SFTP Repository Private Key File Option (--repo-sftp-private-key-file)

SFTP private key file.

SFTP private key file used for authentication.

example: --repo1-sftp-private-key-file=~/.ssh/id_ed25519

SFTP Repository Public Key File Option (--repo-sftp-public-key-file)

SFTP public key file.

Set the SFTP public key file for authentication. This file is optional for builds that use OpenSSL. Other builds require it.

example: --repo1-sftp-public-key-file=~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

Repository Storage CA File Option (--repo-storage-ca-file)

Repository storage CA file.

Use a CA file other than the system default for storage (e.g. S3, Azure) certificates.

example: --repo1-storage-ca-file=/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt

Deprecated Names: repo-azure-ca-file, repo-s3-ca-file

Repository Storage TLS CA Path Option (--repo-storage-ca-path)

Repository storage CA path.

Use a CA path other than the system default for storage (e.g. S3, Azure) certificates.

example: --repo1-storage-ca-path=/etc/pki/tls/certs

Deprecated Names: repo-azure-ca-path, repo-s3-ca-path

Repository Storage Host Option (--repo-storage-host)

Repository storage host.

Connect to a host other than the storage (e.g. S3, Azure) endpoint. This is typically used for testing.

example: --repo1-storage-host=127.0.0.1

Deprecated Names: repo-azure-host, repo-s3-host

Repository Storage Port Option (--repo-storage-port)

Repository storage port.

Port to use when connecting to the storage (e.g. S3, Azure) endpoint (or host if specified).

default: 443
allowed: [1, 65535]
example: --repo1-storage-port=9000

Deprecated Names: repo-azure-port, repo-s3-port

Repository Storage Tag Option (--repo-storage-tag)

Repository storage tag(s).

For an object store repository, such as S3, specify the tags to add to objects. Repeat this option to add multiple tags.

pgBackRest cannot change these tags. Before you run stanza-create, set them correctly to give the entire repository uniform tags.

example: --repo1-storage-tag=key1=value1

Repository Storage Upload Chunk Size Option (--repo-storage-upload-chunk-size)

Repository storage upload chunk size.

Object stores, such as S3, support uploads in chunks for files too large to fit in memory. For smaller files, chunks also reduce the memory used for uploads.

Larger chunks usually improve performance because they reduce upload requests. More files can fit in a single request without division into chunks. However, larger chunks use more memory. Each process needs a chunk buffer, so a larger process-max value also increases total memory use.

Valid chunk sizes depend on the storage type and platform. For example, AWS S3 requires a minimum chunk size of 5MiB. To find minimum and maximum values, search for the term that matches your storage type. Use “part size” for AWS S3, “chunk size” for GCS, and “block size” for Azure.

By default, PostgreSQL creates files no larger than 1GiB. For larger files, pgBackRest increases the chunk size in increments, up to the allowed maximum, to complete the upload.

default (depending on repo-type):
    azure - 4MiB
    gcs - 4MiB
    s3 - 5MiB

allow range (depending on repo-type):
    azure - [4MiB, 1GiB]
    gcs - [4MiB, 1GiB]
    s3 - [5MiB, 1GiB]

example: --repo1-storage-upload-chunk-size=16MiB

Repository Storage Certificate Verify Option (--repo-storage-verify-tls)

Repository storage certificate verify.

Enable or disable verification of the storage server TLS certificate, for example for S3 or Azure. Disable verification only for testing or other cases that use a self-signed certificate.

default: y
example: --no-repo1-storage-verify-tls

Deprecated Names: repo-azure-verify-tls, repo-s3-verify-ssl, repo-s3-verify-tls

Repository Type Option (--repo-type)

Type of storage used for the repository.

The following repository types are supported:

  • azure - Azure Blob Storage Service
  • cifs - Like posix, but disables links and directory fsyncs
  • gcs - Google Cloud Storage
  • posix - Posix-compliant file systems
  • s3 - AWS Simple Storage Service
  • sftp - Secure File Transfer Protocol

For an NFS mount used as a posix repository, follow the PostgreSQL filesystem rules. See Creating a Database Cluster - File Systems.

default: posix
example: --repo1-type=cifs

4.2 - Archive Get Command (archive-get)

Reference for pgBackRest archive-get command options and behavior.

Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: archive-get

PostgreSQL uses this command to restore a backup or perform PITR. It can also use the command instead of streaming to keep a replica current. PostgreSQL needs WAL segments for recovery and replica maintenance.

With multiple repositories, pgBackRest searches for WAL in priority order, such as repo1, then repo2. Usually, give faster or cheaper storage higher priority. If --repo specifies a repository, pgBackRest searches only that repository.

During a restore, pgBackRest generates and configures the archive-get command for PostgreSQL. See the example in Point-in-Time Recovery.

Command Options

Asynchronous Archiving Option (--archive-async)

Push/get WAL segments asynchronously.

Enables asynchronous operation for the archive-push and archive-get commands.

Asynchronous operation can reuse connections and process work in parallel, which improves efficiency. See spool-path, archive-get-queue-max, and archive-push-queue-max for more information.

default: n
example: --archive-async

Maximum Archive Get Queue Size Option (--archive-get-queue-max)

Maximum size of the pgBackRest archive-get queue.

When archive-async is enabled, set the maximum archive-get queue size. pgBackRest stores the queue in spool-path to supply WAL to PostgreSQL faster.

default: 128MiB
allowed: [0B, 4PiB]
example: --archive-get-queue-max=1GiB

Retry Missing WAL Segment Option (--archive-missing-retry)

Retry missing WAL segment

In asynchronous mode, retry a WAL segment that archive-get previously reported as missing. This prevents reuse of spool-path notifications from an earlier restore. Such notifications could cause recovery to fail before consistency is reached.

Disable this option to help PostgreSQL reliably detect the end of archived WAL and switch to streaming from the primary. With retries enabled, a continuous flow of archived WAL keeps PostgreSQL reading the archive instead of switching to streaming.

Before you disable this option, make sure the stanza spool path is empty. The restore command empties it automatically if the spool path is configured at restore time. Otherwise, empty it yourself.

default: y
example: --no-archive-missing-retry

Archive Timeout Option (--archive-timeout)

Archive timeout.

Set the maximum wait, in seconds, for each WAL segment to reach the pgBackRest archive repository. The check and backup commands use this timeout while waiting for WAL segments necessary for backup consistency.

default: 1m
allowed: [100ms, 1d]
example: --archive-timeout=30

General Options

Allow Run as Root Option (--allow-root)

Allow the command to run as the root user.

By default, only restore can run as root because it manages file ownership. Other commands can create root-owned files, for example in the repository. The PostgreSQL user cannot access these files, which causes later commands to fail.

Enable this option to run another command as root. Preferably, run pgBackRest as the user that owns the repository and PostgreSQL cluster.

default: n
example: --allow-root

Buffer Size Option (--buffer-size)

Buffer size for I/O operations.

Set the buffer size for copy, compression, encryption, and other operations. Options determine the number of buffers. Each operation can also use more memory. For example, gz compression can use an additional 256KiB.

Allowed values are 16KiB, 32KiB, 64KiB, 128KiB, 256KiB, 512KiB, 1MiB, 2MiB, 4MiB, 8MiB, and 16MiB.

default: 1MiB
example: --buffer-size=2MiB

pgBackRest Command Option (--cmd)

pgBackRest command.

pgBackRest can generate a command string, for example when restore generates the restore_command setting. It uses the command that started the pgBackRest process unless you specify the cmd option.

CAUTION:

Wrapping the pgBackRest command may cause unpredictable behavior and is not recommended.

default: [path of executed pgbackrest binary]
example: --cmd=/var/lib/pgsql/bin/pgbackrest_wrapper.sh

SSH Client Command Option (--cmd-ssh)

SSH client command.

Use this option to select a different SSH client or when the ssh command is not in $PATH.

default: ssh
example: --cmd-ssh=/usr/bin/ssh

Network Compress Level Option (--compress-level-network)

Network compression level.

Set the network compression level when compress-type=none and the command runs on a host other than the repository host. Compression reduces network traffic. When compress-type is not none, pgBackRest ignores compress-level-network and uses compress-level. This prevents compression of the same file twice.

default: 1
allowed: [-5, 12]
example: --compress-level-network=1

Config Option (--config)

pgBackRest configuration file.

Use this option to select a configuration file other than the default.

default: CFGOPTDEF_CONFIG_PATH "/" PROJECT_CONFIG_FILE
example: --config=/conf/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf

Config Include Path Option (--config-include-path)

Path to additional pgBackRest configuration files.

pgBackRest combines files with the .conf extension in this location with its configuration file. The result is one configuration file.

default: CFGOPTDEF_CONFIG_PATH "/" PROJECT_CONFIG_INCLUDE_PATH
example: --config-include-path=/conf/pgbackrest/conf.d

Config Path Option (--config-path)
